saints.name: St. Pantaleon
saints.title: Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: A physician of Nicomedia who healed without fee and died a martyr under Diocletian…
biography: Pantaleon — in Greek Panteleimon, 'all-compassionate' — was born about 275 at Nicomedia, son of the pagan Eustorgius and the Christian Eubula. Trained in medicine under Euphrosinus, he became physician to the Emperor Maximian, but lapsed until the priest Hermolaus won him back, who showed him Christ the better physician.

He healed a blind man by invoking the name of Jesus, converted his father, freed his slaves, and treated the poor without fee. Denounced by envious colleagues in the persecution of Diocletian, he confessed Christ before the emperor, healed a paralytic in proof, and after torments was beheaded about the year 305.

His martyrdom is attested early: Theodoret preached on him before 457, the Martyrology of St. Jerome names him, and Justinian rebuilt his shrine at Nicomedia. In the East he is honored among the Holy Unmercenaries, the unpaid physicians; in the West, after the Black Death, among the Fourteen Holy Helpers.

Healing freely for Christ's sake, he is patron of physicians and of the sick. At Ravello in Italy a phial of his blood, like that of St. Januarius, is said to liquefy on his feast, as St. Alphonsus Liguori testified he had seen.
saints.knownFor: Healing the poor without fee and his martyrdom under Diocletian.
